subject: microbiology
title: Streptococcus pyogenes: Lancefield Grouping and Beta Haemolysis

steps.tx: **Streptococcus pyogenes** is group A streptococcus: gram positive cocci in chains, catalase negative, beta haemolytic (complete clear zone) on blood agar, bacitracin susceptible, PYR positive, armed with M protein, hyaluronic acid capsule and a toxin cupboard, causing pharyngitis, skin sepsis, scarlet fever, necrotising fasciitis and the immune sequelae rheumatic fever and glomerulonephritis.
steps.say: Chains, catalase negative, beta haemolysis, group A: pyogenes identified and feared in one line.

vis.alt: Streptococci laboratory classification plates showing haemolysis patterns
vis.caption: Streptococcal laboratory classification by haemolysis, group A beta haemolytic.

steps.tx: **Lancefield grouping** sorts beta haemolytic streptococci by cell wall carbohydrate antigens (Rebecca Lancefield's serology): A pyogenes, B agalactiae, C and G dysgalactiae kin, extracted and agglutinated with antisera or latex kits at bench. Alpha haemolytic streptococci mostly escape grouping (pneumococcus and viridans identified otherwise).
steps.say: Wall carbohydrate letters assign beta haemolytic streptococci their clinical tribes.

left.title: Lancefield roster
points: C and G: S dysgalactiae and anginosus kin
D historically: enterococci removed to own genus

right.title: Grouping methods
points: Extraction enzymes free the C carbohydrate
MALDI increasingly first, grouping for epidemiology

steps.tx: **Beta haemolysis** (complete clearing by streptolysins, oxygen labile O and stable S) distinguishes pyogenes colonies (pinpoint with wide clear zones, subsurface stab showing O activity) from alpha greening viridans and pneumococcus. Haemolysis reading needs sheep blood, good light and humility about enterococcal mimics.
steps.say: Clear zone, pinpoint colony: beta haemolysis is pyogenes waving from the plate.

left.title: Haemolysis reads
points: Alpha: partial, green (hydrogen peroxide and pneumolysin)
Stab culture reveals oxygen labile haemolysin

right.title: Plate discipline
points: Mixed throat flora needs selective media history
Confirm A by bacitracin, PYR or latex

steps.tx: **M protein** is pyogenes' antiphagocytic fibrillar spear (over 200 emm types), blocking complement deposition, typing strains epidemiologically, and supplying rheumatic fever's mimicry antigens shared with cardiac tissue. Hyaluronic acid capsule (host identical, non immunogenic) adds stealth in invasive strains, mucoid colonies warning of them.
steps.say: M protein repels phagocytes, types strains and mimics heart tissue: one molecule, three examinations.

right.title: Capsule facts
points: Hyaluronic acid identical to host connective
Hyaluronidase own spreading factor dissolves it

steps.tx: **M protein** is the fibrillar antiphagocytic spear of Streptococcus pyogenes, with more than 200 emm types. It blocks complement from depositing on the bacterial surface, so phagocytes fail. The same typing system tracks strains in outbreaks. Parts of M protein mimic cardiac tissue, which is the molecular background of rheumatic fever. Invasive strains often add a hyaluronic acid capsule identical to host material and therefore poorly immunogenic. Mucoid colonies on the plate are the visible warning of that capsule.
steps.say: M protein of Streptococcus pyogenes, in more than 200 emm types, blocks complement deposition and phagocytosis and is used to type strains. Shared sequences with heart tissue underlie rheumatic fever. A hyaluronic capsule like host tissue adds stealth in invasive strains and can look mucoid on agar.

vis.alt: A diagram shows M protein fibrils on a streptococcal surface blocking complement deposition and phagocyte contact.
vis.caption: Fibrillar M protein stands off the cell wall, complement fails to deposit, and the phagocyte cannot get a grip. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Pharyngitis diagnosis** balances culture, rapid antigen and clinical scores: throat culture on blood agar remains sensitive standard, rapid antigen detection specific but sensitivity limited (children negative backed by culture), anti DNase B and ASO serving retrospective and sequelae questions rather than acute sore throat decisions.
steps.say: Rapid antigen rules in, culture rescues negatives in children; antibodies answer last month's throat.

left.title: Acute tools
points: Culture backup in children and adolescents

right.title: Retrospective tools
points: ASO titres for rheumatic fever support
Anti DNase B better after skin infection
Antibodies never start acute antibiotics alone

steps.tx: **Scarlet fever and toxin skin** preview the toxin lessons: erythrogenic (pyrogenic) exotoxins A to C, phage borne superantigens, produce scarlatiniform rash, strawberry tongue and Pastia lines in toxin naive hosts, while streptococcal toxic shock and necrotising fasciitis use the same cupboard at invasive scale.
steps.say: Phage toxins paint scarlet fever; the same cupboard shocks and necrotises when invasive.

left.title: Toxin roster preview
points: Streptolysins O and S haemolyse and kill cells
DNases thin pus (anti DNase B marker)

right.title: Invasive syndromes
points: Necrotising fasciitis: pain out of proportion
Streptococcal toxic shock: IVIG and clindamycin adjuncts

steps.tx: **Penicillin loyalty** defines pyogenes uniquely: no confirmed penicillin resistance anywhere despite a century of use (intrinsic target stability, fitness), macrolide and clindamycin resistance variable by region (the toxin adjunct checked), tetracycline resistance common. Rheumatic fever prevention (treating pharyngitis, but not reliably post skin infection GN) justifies antibiotic insistence in sore throats at risk.
steps.say: Pyogenes never learned penicillin resistance; prescribe it with a century's confidence.

right.title: Why treat pharyngitis
points: Prevent rheumatic fever (9 day window tradition)

steps.tx: **Carriage and outbreaks** complicate throats: asymptomatic pharyngeal carriage (up to a fifth of schoolchildren in winter) makes positive tests in viral illness ambiguous, food borne and post surgical outbreaks type by emm and genome, and rheumatic fever programmes in endemic regions still debate benzathine penicillin prophylaxis adherence, carrier treatment in defined outbreaks and rheumatic recurrences.
steps.say: A positive swab in a coughing, runny nosed child may be carriage wearing a viral costume.

left.title: Carrier reality
points: Carriers low transmission and sequelae risk
Exceptions: outbreaks, rheumatic households, invasive contacts rules

right.title: Public health
points: Vaccine hope on conserved M and non M antigens
